findings.issue_text: flusher.py (join): per-process wait loop breaks on deadline expiry, skipping remaining processes so they are never waited on or terminate()d, leaving orphaned flusher processes and their Redis connections after timeout

flusher.py (__init__): `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats max_processes=0 as unlimited instead of an explicit value; should use `if max_processes is None` semantics
flusher.py (wait_produce timer): tag key is "shards" here but "shard" in produce/segment_size_bytes timers for the same value, producing inconsistent metric series and splitting dashboards/alerts

flusher.py (metrics tags): tagging spans.buffer.flusher.produce, segment_size_bytes, and wait_produce with comma-joined shard lists creates high-cardinality metric series (one per shard grouping), a cardinality blowup for statsd backends

flusher.py (_create_process_for_shards): on restart a new SpansBuffer(shards) is constructed while the original factory buffer becomes unused for record_stored_segments/get_memory_info; repeated registration/connection setup per restart
test_consumer.py:60-63: fixed time.sleep(0.1) race-condition workaround may be insufficient on loaded CI, making the test flaky; no synchronization/polling for the expected condition
test_consumer.py: no test covers restart behavior with multiple processes (_ensure_processes_alive, restart-count RuntimeError, shard-map preservation across restarts), the core new logic of the PR
flusher.py (_create_process_for_shard): dead code — never called, loop-restart semantics differ from actual restart path; will rot and mislead readers

flusher.py (submit): restarted process gets fresh process_healthy_since while pending segments may already be past max_unhealthy_seconds, allowing kill→healthy→hang restart loops up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS with no backpressure signal carried, delaying MessageRejected detection

flusher.py (submit, memory check): memory info aggregated over per-shard buffers could double-count shards if a shard appears in more than one buffer or a buffer is created during a restart race; the invariant is only implicit

CLAUDE.md:448-456: example labels hasattr() as WRONG for unions, but hasattr works at runtime for str | None; the real rationale (static type-narrowing/mypy) is not stated, making the guidance misleading

goldens.comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: flusher.py (__init__): `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats max_processes=0 as unlimited instead of an explicit value; should use `if max_processes is None` semantics

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, the diff sets `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, so an explicit `max_processes=0` (possible since the new click option is `type=int` with no validation) will be treated the same as `None` and fall back to `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. This is a real, diff-grounded edge-case/semantics issue (should likely be `if max_processes is None` or validate `>=1`), but it’s not clearly a verifiable defect without a spec that 0 is meaningful/allowed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: flusher.py (metrics tags): tagging spans.buffer.flusher.produce, segment_size_bytes, and wait_produce with comma-joined shard lists creates high-cardinality metric series (one per shard grouping), a cardinality blowup for statsd backends

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, the diff adds metric tags using `shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))` and then tags `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, and `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})`. Since `shard_tag` is a comma-joined list representing the *set of shards assigned to a process*, this can create many distinct tag values across varying shard-to-process assignments (especially with `max_processes` causing shard grouping). That’s a concrete, diff-grounded operational concern (metrics cardinality blowup), not a direct correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: flusher.py (_create_process_for_shards): on restart a new SpansBuffer(shards) is constructed while the original factory buffer becomes unused for record_stored_segments/get_memory_info; repeated registration/connection setup per restart

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `_create_process_for_shards` now constructs a new `SpansBuffer(shards)` every time a process is (re)created and stores it in `self.buffers[process_index]` (overwriting any prior buffer) without any visible cleanup of the prior buffer. Also, `SpanFlusher.__init__` no longer assigns `self.buffer = buffer`, and later calls to `record_stored_segments()` / `get_memory_info()` iterate only over `self.buffers.values()`, so the original `buffer` passed into `SpanFlusher` is only used for `assigned_shards` during initialization and then effectively unused. Whether this causes real resource leaks/connection re-registration can’t be proven from the diff alone (depends on `SpansBuffer` internals), but the concern is specific and directly grounded in the new restart logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test_consumer.py:60-63: fixed time.sleep(0.1) race-condition workaround may be insufficient on loaded CI, making the test flaky; no synchronization/polling for the expected condition

adjudication.rationale: In `test_basic`, the new `time.sleep(0.1)` (lines ~60-63) is intended to “give flusher threads time to process”, but earlier in the same test `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` replaces `time.sleep` globally, so this sleep is a no-op and provides no synchronization at all. Even aside from that, the test uses a fixed sleep rather than waiting/polling for a condition, which can make it flaky under load. This reliability issue is directly introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test_consumer.py: no test covers restart behavior with multiple processes (_ensure_processes_alive, restart-count RuntimeError, shard-map preservation across restarts), the core new logic of the PR

adjudication.rationale: The PR introduces significant new restart/health logic in `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive` (per-process `process_restarts` dict, per-process `healthy_since`/`backpressure_since`, and restart via `_create_process_for_shards` using `process_to_shards_map`). The added tests (`test_flusher_processes_limit`, updated assertions in `test_flusher`) only validate process limiting/shard distribution and backpressure aggregation, not the new multi-process restart behavior (e.g., a dead/hung process triggers restart, restart-count `RuntimeError`, or that shard→process mapping is preserved across restarts). This is a specific, diff-grounded testing gap rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: flusher.py (_create_process_for_shard): dead code — never called, loop-restart semantics differ from actual restart path; will rot and mislead readers

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, the method `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is added but there is no call site for it in the shown diff (restart logic in `_ensure_processes_alive` directly calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`). This makes `_create_process_for_shard` effectively dead/unreferenced within the PR and likely to rot/mislead readers about the intended restart path. This is a maintainability issue rather than a directly verifiable runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: flusher.py (submit): restarted process gets fresh process_healthy_since while pending segments may already be past max_unhealthy_seconds, allowing kill→healthy→hang restart loops up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS with no backpressure signal carried, delaying MessageRejected detection

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly preserves backpressure state across restarts: `_create_process_for_shards` only resets `process_healthy_since[process_index]` and keeps `process_backpressure_since[process_index]` (comment: “Keep back pressure across the restart, however.”). `submit()` also checks all `process_backpressure_since` values and raises `MessageRejected` if any exceeds the configured threshold. While `process_healthy_since` being reset can delay hang detection until `max-unhealthy-seconds`, that behavior already existed in the pre-change single-process version (it reset `healthy_since` on restart) and the finding’s claim of “no backpressure signal carried” is contradicted by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: flusher.py (submit, memory check): memory info aggregated over per-shard buffers could double-count shards if a shard appears in more than one buffer or a buffer is created during a restart race; the invariant is only implicit

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit`, memory info is aggregated by iterating `self.buffers.values()` after `_ensure_processes_alive()`. From the diff, each shard is assigned exactly once into `process_to_shards_map` (single pass over `buffer.assigned_shards`), and each `process_index` has exactly one entry in `self.buffers` (a dict overwritten on restart via `self.buffers[process_index] = shard_buffer`). There is no diff-evident path where the same shard can exist in more than one *current* buffer in `self.buffers`, nor a restart race that would cause double-counting in this aggregation (old buffers may exist elsewhere, but they are not included in the dict iteration).

adjudication_records.issue_text: CLAUDE.md:448-456: example labels hasattr() as WRONG for unions, but hasattr works at runtime for str | None; the real rationale (static type-narrowing/mypy) is not stated, making the guidance misleading

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a CLAUDE.md guideline labeling `hasattr()` as "WRONG" for `str | None` and `isinstance(x, str)` as "RIGHT" without explaining the intended rationale (static type narrowing / mypy). As written, it’s misleading because `hasattr(x, "replace")` is valid runtime behavior for a `str | None` union and will work for the shown example; the doc guidance needs clarification to be accurate/actionable.
